summary: Paul David Numrich works in religious and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Michigan in 1992 and held posts at Loyola University Chicago and the Theological Consortium of Greater Columbus (both attested 2006).

Paul Debes (1906–2004) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Nyanatiloka Mahathera (1931–1932). He founded the Buddhistisches Seminar (1948), Buddhistische Gesellschaft Hamburg (1954), Wissen und Wandel (1955), and Deutsche Buddhistische Gesellschaft (1955).

Paul Demiéville (1894–1979) was a Sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Sorbonne and under Lévi, Chavannes, Meillet, Cabaton, and Pelliot. He held posts at Xiamen University, INALCO, EPHE (1945–1957), and Collège de France (1946–1964).

Paul Deussen (1845–1919) was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at Bonn, Tübingen, and Berlin, completing his habilitation under Eduard Zeller. He taught as a Privatdocent at Berlin (1881–1887) and became a professor at Kiel University in 1889.

Paul Dundas (1952–2023) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Edinburgh and under Michael Coulson. He led Asian Studies at the University of Edinburgh (~1976–2017) and served as head of the Pali Text Society (~2002–2023).

Paul E. Muller-Ortega is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who was a doctoral student at the University of California, Santa Barbara. He taught in the Department of Religion and Classics at the University of Rochester (attested 2000).
Paul Ekman (1934–2025) studied at New York University (~1952–1954) and Adelphi University (~1954–1958). He held a post at the University of California, San Francisco, from approximately 1960 to 2004.

Paul F. Knitter (1939–) is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University (~1958–1966) and the University of Marburg (~1968–1972), later holding a post at Union Theological Seminary (~2007–2016).

Paul Fredericq (1850–1920) was a historian who completed his teacher's exam and doctorate at the University of Liège and studied at Ghent. He was a professor at Liège (~1879–1883), and at Ghent from 1883, serving as rector in 1919.

Paul Fuller is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Bristol (1998–2003) under Rupert Gethin and Paul Dundas, later lecturing at Sydney (2008–2011), Cardiff (2015), and Edinburgh (attested 2026).

Paul G. Brewster (1898–) studied at Oakland City University and the University of Oklahoma. An Indologist, he taught at Tennessee (1926–1929), UNC Chapel Hill (1929–1930), Shurtleff College (1948–1949), Henderson State (1949–1952), and Tennessee Technological University (1954).

Paul G. Hackett specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a curator and bibliographer at the University of Virginia (attested 1994, 2003) and later held research and lecturing posts at Columbia University (attested 2003, 2016).

Paul Goldschmidt (1850–1877) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Heidelberg, Tübingen, Berlin, and Göttingen, supervised by Theodor Benfey, Rudolf von Roth, and Albrecht Weber. In 1874, he was appointed epigraphist to the Government of Ceylon.
Paul Greenough is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago (1968–1977) and joined the history faculty at the University of Iowa in 1974.

Paul Groner is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar who earned his PhD from Yale and studied at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa. He was appointed to the religious studies faculty at the University of Virginia (attested 1982–2026).

Paul Hacker (1913–1979) was an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar who completed his PhD at Berlin and habilitation at Bonn under Willibald Kirfel. He held chairs of Indology at Bonn (1955–1963) and Münster (1963–1978).

Paul Harrison is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Auckland and earned a PhD at ANU (~1974–1979) under Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana. He taught at Auckland, Canterbury, and Stanford (~2007).

Paul Hershman (1950–1976) was an Indologist and anthropologist who studied at the London School of Economics (~1972–1976). He served as a Lecturer in Anthropology at the University of Sussex (~1975–1976).
Paul Hoornaert is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who taught Mikaël Bauer and held an academic post at Kanazawa University (attested 1991–2002).

Paul Horn (1863–1908) was an Iranian and Central Asian studies linguist. He earned his PhD at Halle-Wittenberg under Christian Bartholomae and studied at Berlin, later serving as Privatdozent (1889) and associate professor (1900) at the University of Strasbourg.
